title: Repeats in a Family
statement: Let $P(x)=x^2-31x+198$ and $Q(x)=x^2-27x+170$. There are exactly two real numbers $\lambda$ for which the polynomial $P(x)+\lambda Q(x)$ has a repeated real root. Let $r_1$ and $r_2$ be the repeated roots corresponding to these two values of $\lambda$. Find $r_1^2+r_2^2$.
hints: Look at the one member of the family that is not quadratic: taking $\lambda=-1$ gives $P(x)-Q(x)$, which is linear. Find its root, then evaluate $P$ and $Q$ at that point.

The root of $P-Q$ is $x=7$, and $P(7)=Q(7)=30$. Make the variable substitution $u=x-7$, so that $P$ and $Q$ have the same constant term in $u$. Then consider what Vieta's formula for the product of the roots says about every quadratic member of the family.

With $u=x-7$, we have $P+\lambda Q=(1+\lambda)(u^2+30)-(17+13\lambda)u$. For $\lambda\ne -1$ the product of the roots in $u$ is $30$, so a repeated root satisfies $u^2=30$. Convert these values of $u$ back to $x$.
solution:
Put $u=x-7$. Then $P=u^2-17u+30$ and $Q=u^2-13u+30$, so
$$P+\lambda Q=(1+\lambda)(u^2+30)-(17+13\lambda)u.$$

If $\lambda=-1$ this is $-4u$, which has no repeated root. Otherwise it is a quadratic in $u$ with root product $30$. A repeated root $u_0$ then satisfies $u_0^2=30$, so $u_0=\pm\sqrt{30}$.

Each sign does occur. The polynomial equals $(1+\lambda)(u-u_0)^2$ exactly when $17+13\lambda=2u_0(1+\lambda)$, that is $(13-2u_0)\lambda=2u_0-17$. Since $2u_0$ is irrational, $13-2u_0\ne0$, so there is exactly one such $\lambda$. It is not $-1$, since $\lambda=-1$ gives $4$ on the left and $0$ on the right. Hence the two values of $\lambda$ give $u_0=\pm\sqrt{30}$.

The repeated roots are $r_{1,2}=7\pm\sqrt{30}$, so
$$r_1^2+r_2^2=2(49+30)=158.$$
